title: A72 Traceability Matrix row
description: Schema for one row of analysis/canonical/core_controls/A72_traceability_matrix.csv (Phase 3, US-S8-02). Each row is a single Story↔Claim↔Source link triple; the matrix is a JOIN over A70 + A59 + A50, with one row per traceable connection. Producer: bsa-traceability-matrix (pure derivation skill — never authors net-new content; rejects rows whose IDs don't resolve in upstream artifacts). Consumers: bsa-backlog-bridge (uses the matrix to attach claim/source provenance to exported stories), and human reviewers querying for orphan / coverage gaps. Cross-field invariants are documentary at this layer (cross-artifact lookups outside F5's path-bound dispatch); the skill self-validates before write.

TraceID.description: Stable identifier TR-NNN, TR-NNNN, or TR-XXX-NNNN (category prefix). Matrices on large engagements can grow into the thousands of triples (one Story may legitimately fan out to dozens of Claims, each of which traces to a Source); the 5-digit form keeps headroom without forcing renumbering.

StoryID.description: Singular A70 story ID. Composite trace rows are forbidden — one row = one Story↔Claim↔Source triple. If a story relates to multiple claims, emit multiple A72 rows.

ClaimID.description: Singular A59 claim ID. Same singularity discipline as StoryID.

SourceID.description: Singular A50 source ID. Same singularity discipline. Cross-artifact integrity (this SourceID must equal the ClaimID's own SourceID in A59) is the skill's responsibility — F5's path-bound dispatch can't naturally reach a sibling artifact at write time. The consistency rule applies to EVERY row regardless of LinkType (a51-routed rows defer ACCEPTANCE, not ID resolution).

LinkType.description: How the Story↔Claim link was established. 'direct' — A70.SourceClaimIDs explicitly listed this ClaimID. 'nfr-mediated' — derived through a transitive A62 NFR (story relates to NFR via RelatedNFRIDs; NFR's SourceClaimIDs lists this ClaimID). When the SAME (Story, Claim, Source) triple is reachable both directly and via NFR-mediation, emit ONE 'direct' row only — the matrix's row identity is the triple itself; multi-route reachability is annotated in traceability_coverage.md, not duplicated as multiple A72 rows. 'a51-routed' — the trace is fully resolved (all three IDs known + claim-source consistency satisfied) but acceptance is deferred (e.g., link strength contested, claim under review); MUST co-populate A51Ref via x-bsa-deferral-rules. Unresolved IDs never appear in A72 — those go to traceability_orphans.md + an A51 'missing_source' route only.

LinkStrength.description: Confidence in the link. Default: derive from the upstream A59 claim's ClaimStrength × A50 source's ReliabilityTier (T1/T2 → high; T3 → medium; T4/T5 → low). Operator may explicitly override (raise OR lower) with A51 rationale.

A51Ref.description: Optional A51 cross-reference. REQUIRED (non-empty) when LinkType == 'a51-routed' — every routed-trace row must have a decision / action route recorded in A51 (parallel to A70.INVESTStatus + A71.AutomationStatus deferral patterns). Enforced at the cross-field level (x-bsa-deferral-rules).

x-bsa-csv-columns-order._comment: Canonical column order for diff stability.

x-bsa-uniqueness-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer as of v1.2.12 via governance/schemas/write_validator.py::_apply_uniqueness_rules. Schema-agnostic generic extension (see v1.2.10 CHANGELOG). Every A72 row is a distinct story-claim-source triple binding; duplicate TraceIDs would let two distinct traces collapse into one. Pre-v1.2.12 duplicate TraceIDs were caught only at fixture-review time; v1.2.12 makes it mechanical at hook time.
x-bsa-uniqueness-rules.rationale: Without this rule, duplicate TraceID values could land at promote-gate + silently break every downstream cross-reference. TraceID is the row-identifier.

x-bsa-deferral-rules._comment: Generalized status+A51-coupling pattern (mirrors A71.x-bsa-deferral-rules; same _apply_deferral_rules handler in write_validator.py). LinkType == 'a51-routed' MUST co-populate A51Ref. Configurable via status_field override (the handler defaults to AutomationStatus for A71; we override to LinkType here).
x-bsa-deferral-rules.rationale: A trace row marked a51-routed without an A51 route is an undocumented punt — the gap appears later in coverage reports with no decision trail. Co-populating A51Ref keeps the routing explicit.

x-bsa-foreign-key-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer as of v1.1.3 (closes TODO-S8-02-X-ARTIFACT-FK). EVERY A72 row's StoryID, ClaimID, and SourceID MUST resolve to an existing row in the corresponding canonical artifact (A70 / A59 / A50) — including a51-routed rows (those defer ACCEPTANCE, not ID resolution). Additionally, the row's ClaimID's own SourceID (per A59) MUST equal this row's SourceID — the matrix join must be internally consistent. The applies_to_all_rows flag is an explicit pin: any future loosening that exempts a LinkType class from FK/consistency would be a contract regression. Implementation: governance/schemas/write_validator.py::_apply_foreign_key_rules + _SiblingArtifactCache (per-validation-run memoized sibling reads from analysis/canonical/core_controls/). Pre-v1.1.3 enforcement was bsa-traceability-matrix self-validation only; v1.1.3 makes the rule mechanical at hook time so any writer (orchestrator, skill, operator manual edit) is gated. Same shape as A71's x-bsa-nfr-coverage-rules.
x-bsa-foreign-key-rules.rationale: Without this rule, the skill could emit phantom traces: TraceID rows pointing at StoryIDs that don't exist or at Claim/Source pairs that A59 disagrees with. The whole point of the matrix is mechanical traceability; an unverified join defeats it.

x-bsa-foreign-key-refs._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer as of v1.3.7 (closes the stale-A51Ref gap surfaced in the v1.3.6 output review). Parallel to A59 / A60 / A62 / A70 / A71 — every A51Ref column MUST resolve in A51_issue_route_register.csv. A72's older x-bsa-foreign-key-rules covers Story/Claim/Source resolution but not A51Ref; the deferral rule (x-bsa-deferral-rules above) only checks that A51Ref is non-blank when LinkType=a51-routed, NOT that the value points to an actual A51 row. Without this addition, an a51-routed trace can carry a non-blank but stale A51Ref (e.g., A51-007 typed when the register only has rows up to A51-005) and silently propagate through downstream coverage reports. Generic refs handler + multi=true matches the A51Ref column pattern (single-or-list with `;` / `/` delimiter).

foreign_keys.rationale: When the trace row is a51-routed, A51Ref MUST resolve in A51_issue_route_register.csv. Blank A51Ref is allowed (the deferral-rules extension above gates the non-blank requirement when LinkType=a51-routed).
